about: Golden Set version 2 (ADR 0012, docs/golden-set.md): version 1's cases other than the brief's, rewritten with one-claim Required Facts in two tiers, and new cases, each recording its split. Version 1 (golden_set.json) stays unchanged as a record.
split_rule: Each case records its split, and no case ever moves. Version 1's cases rewritten here keep their ids and are dev. New cases are pending until all of them exist; then the 20 whose ids have the lowest SHA-256 hex digests (UTF-8) are holdout and the rest dev. A run refuses while any case is pending.

cases.question: What legal proceedings does Apple disclose in its latest Filings?
cases.notes: Section hint: Legal Proceedings. "Latest" is the FY2025 10-K plus the Q1 FY2026 10-Q, which adds the Ninth Circuit ruling. Rewritten for version 2 from the whole Legal Proceedings Section of both Filings: the European Commission's DMA investigations, the DOJ lawsuit and Epic Games are must-state; the Article 6(4) investigation, the appeals, the contempt referral and the other proceedings are details. The EUR 500 million fine is in euros, so the figure check does not apply.

required_facts.fact: Apple was fined €500 million by the European Commission on April 23, 2025 in its Digital Markets Act Article 5(4) investigation.
required_facts.evidence: On April 23, 2025, the Commission fined the Company €500 million in the Article 5(4) Investigation

required_facts.fact: Apple has appealed the European Commission's Article 5(4) decision under the Digital Markets Act.
required_facts.evidence: The Company has appealed the Commission’s Article 5(4) decision.

required_facts.fact: Apple says the European Commission's Article 5(4) decision included a cease and desist order requiring it to remove restrictions that prevent developers from steering users outside the App Store.
required_facts.evidence: issued a cease and desist order requiring the Company to remove technical and commercial restrictions that prevent developers from steering users to alternative distribution channels outside the App Store

required_facts.fact: Apple says the European Commission issued preliminary findings in its Digital Markets Act Article 6(4) investigation on April 23, 2025.
required_facts.evidence: Also on April 23, 2025, the Commission issued preliminary findings in the Article 6(4) Investigation.

required_facts.fact: Apple says a final finding of violation in the Article 6(4) investigation could bring fines of up to 10% of its annual worldwide net sales.
required_facts.evidence: may impose fines up to 10% of the Company’s annual worldwide net sales

required_facts.fact: Apple faces a civil antitrust lawsuit filed by the DOJ and state attorneys general on March 21, 2024.
required_facts.evidence: On March 21, 2024, the DOJ and a number of state and district attorneys general filed a civil antitrust lawsuit

required_facts.fact: Apple says the DOJ lawsuit alleges monopolization or attempted monopolization of the markets for performance smartphones and smartphones.
required_facts.evidence: alleging monopolization or attempted monopolization in the markets for “performance smartphones” and “smartphones” in violation of U.S. antitrust laws

required_facts.fact: Apple says it believes it has substantial defenses against the DOJ lawsuit and intends to vigorously defend itself.
required_facts.evidence: The Company believes it has substantial defenses and intends to vigorously defend itself.

required_facts.fact: Apple faces various civil lawsuits in U.S. state and federal courts alleging antitrust violations similar to the DOJ's and seeking monetary damages.
required_facts.evidence: various civil litigation matters have been filed in state and federal courts in the U.S. alleging similar violations of U.S. antitrust laws and seeking monetary damages and other nonmonetary relief

required_facts.fact: In the Epic Games case, a California court found on April 30, 2025 that Apple had violated the 2021 Injunction.
required_facts.evidence: On April 30, 2025, the California District Court found the Company to be in violation of the 2021 Injunction

required_facts.fact: Apple says the California District Court referred it to the U.S. Attorney to determine whether criminal contempt proceedings are appropriate.
required_facts.evidence: referred the Company to the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of California for a determination whether criminal contempt proceedings are appropriate

required_facts.fact: On December 11, 2025 the Ninth Circuit upheld in part the 2025 Injunction against Apple in the Epic Games case.
required_facts.evidence: On December 11, 2025, the Ninth Circuit Court issued an order upholding the 2025 Injunction in part

required_facts.fact: Apple says the Ninth Circuit held that it can charge a commission on link-out purchases.
required_facts.evidence: The Ninth Circuit Court also held that the Company can charge a commission on link-out purchases

required_facts.fact: Apple says the Ninth Circuit's order allows it to require parity in size, form and placement between its in-app purchase and links to outside purchases.
required_facts.evidence: modifying certain aspects to allow the Company to require parity in size, form and placement between the Company’s in-app purchase and any links for consumers to make purchases outside an app

required_facts.fact: Apple's deadline to petition for rehearing of the Ninth Circuit's order is March 2, 2026.
required_facts.evidence: The deadline for the Company to file a petition for rehearing is March 2, 2026.

required_facts.fact: Apple says it settled certain other matters in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 that were not material individually or in the aggregate.
required_facts.evidence: The Company settled certain matters during the first quarter of 2026 that did not individually or in the aggregate have a material impact on the Company’s financial condition or operating results.

cases.question: What foreign currency and interest rate risks does Coca-Cola disclose in its latest annual report?
cases.notes: Section hint: Market Risk (10-K Item 7A). Coca-Cola's latest 10-K is FY2024. Rewritten for version 2 from the whole Market Risk Section's foreign currency and interest rate passages; the commodity price passage is outside the question. The Section's dollar amounts ($28.7 billion of revenue outside the U.S., $18,442 million of notional value, the sensitivity estimates) have no SEC company-facts value, so the facts that rest on them state no amount; the amounts stay in the evidence.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola uses derivative financial instruments primarily to reduce its exposure to adverse fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates, interest rates and other market risks.
required_facts.evidence: Our Company uses derivative financial instruments primarily to reduce our exposure to adverse fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates, interest rates, commodity prices and other market risks.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola says it does not enter into derivative financial instruments for trading purposes.
required_facts.evidence: We do not enter into derivative financial instruments for trading purposes.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola manages most of its foreign currency exposures on a consolidated basis, which lets it net certain exposures and use natural offsets.
required_facts.evidence: We manage most of our foreign currency exposures on a consolidated basis, which allows us to net certain exposures and take advantage of any natural offsets.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola generated part of its 2024 net operating revenues from operations outside the United States.
required_facts.evidence: In 2024, we generated $28.7 billion of our net operating revenues from operations outside the United States.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola says the geographic diversity of its operations means weakness in some currencies may be offset by strength in others over time.
required_facts.evidence: Due to the geographic diversity of our operations, weakness in some currencies may be offset by strength in other currencies over time.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola hedges portions of its forecasted foreign currency cash flows with forward exchange contracts and foreign currency options and collars.
required_facts.evidence: Our Company enters into forward exchange contracts and purchases foreign currency options and collars (principally euro, British pound and Japanese yen) to hedge certain portions of forecasted cash flows denominated in foreign currencies.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola's foreign currency hedges are principally in the euro, British pound and Japanese yen.
required_facts.evidence: (principally euro, British pound and Japanese yen)

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola also uses forward exchange contracts to hedge its net investments in foreign operations.
required_facts.evidence: We also enter into forward exchange contracts as hedges of net investments in foreign operations.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola discloses the total notional value of its foreign currency derivatives as of December 31, 2024.
required_facts.evidence: The total notional values of our foreign currency derivatives were $18,442 million and $17,505 million as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola estimates that a 10% weakening of the U.S. dollar would have decreased the fair value of its foreign currency derivatives that qualified for hedge accounting.
required_facts.evidence: The fair value of foreign currency derivatives that qualified for hedge accounting resulted in a net unrealized gain of $366 million as of December 31, 2024, and we estimate that a 10% weakening of the U.S. dollar would have resulted in a $511 million decrease in fair value.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola says it is subject to interest rate volatility on its existing and future issuances of debt.
required_facts.evidence: The Company is subject to interest rate volatility with regard to existing and future issuances of debt.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola enters into interest rate swap agreements from time to time to manage its exposure to interest rate fluctuations.
required_facts.evidence: From time to time, we enter into interest rate swap agreements to manage our exposure to interest rate fluctuations.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola monitors its mix of fixed-rate and variable-rate debt.
required_facts.evidence: We monitor our mix of fixed-rate and variable-rate debt as well as our mix of short-term debt and long-term debt.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola estimates that a 1 percentage point increase in interest rates would have increased its 2024 interest expense.
required_facts.evidence: we estimate that a 1 percentage point increase in interest rates would have increased interest expense by $127 million in 2024

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola says it is subject to interest rate risk on its investments in highly liquid debt securities.
required_facts.evidence: The Company is subject to interest rate risk related to its investments in highly liquid debt securities.

required_facts.fact: Coca-Cola's policy requires its investments in highly liquid debt securities to be investment grade.
required_facts.evidence: Our policy requires these investments to be investment grade, with the primary objective of minimizing the risk of principal loss.

cases.question: What cybersecurity risks does UnitedHealth describe in its latest annual report?
cases.notes: UnitedHealth's latest 10-K is FY2024; the Change Healthcare cyberattack is in both Risk Factors and MD&A. Rewritten for version 2 from the whole cyber passages of Risk Factors and MD&A, plus the Cybersecurity Section (Item 1C), which version 1 left out. The cyberattack's cost figures (direct response costs, business disruption, loans to care providers) have no SEC company-facts value, so their facts state no amount.

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth says its Change Healthcare business was subject to a cyberattack in 2024.
required_facts.evidence: we previously reported our Change Healthcare business, which we had recently acquired, was subject to a cyberattack in 2024

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth says the data involved in the Change Healthcare cyberattack contained protected health information or personally identifiable information.
required_facts.evidence: in which the data involved contained protected health information or personally identifiable information.

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth says it is regularly the target of attempted cyberattacks and other security threats.
required_facts.evidence: We are regularly the target of attempted cyberattacks  and other security threats

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth says cyberattacks or data security incidents at it or at third parties it relies on could cause lost revenue, increased costs, significant liability and reputational harm.
required_facts.evidence: If we or third parties we rely on sustain cyberattacks or other privacy or data security incidents resulting in disruption to our operations or the disclosure of protected personal information or proprietary or confidential information, we could suffer a loss of revenue and increased costs, negative operational effects, exposure to significant liability, reputational harm and other serious negative consequences.

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth expects to continue to experience data security incidents despite its programs to detect, contain and respond to them.
required_facts.evidence: we expect that we will continue to experience these incidents, some of which may negatively affect our business

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth says techniques used to obtain unauthorized access are increasing in sophistication, in part due to evolving AI technologies.
required_facts.evidence: because the techniques used to obtain unauthorized access, disable or degrade service, or sabotage systems change frequently and are increasing in sophistication, in part due to use of evolving AI/ML technologies (including generative AI)

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth says recently acquired or non-integrated businesses have brought heightened cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
required_facts.evidence: There have previously been and may be in the future heightened vulnerabilities due to recently-acquired or non-integrated businesses.

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth says the third-party vendors it relies on to process its data face similar risks outside its direct oversight and control.
required_facts.evidence: The operations of these vendors are subject to similar risks, but are outside our direct oversight and control.

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth says the costs to eliminate or address security threats and vulnerabilities could be material.
required_facts.evidence: The costs to eliminate or address the foregoing security threats and vulnerabilities before or after a cybersecurity incident could be material.

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth says a privacy or security breach could result in significant fines, penalties and litigation awards.
required_facts.evidence: could also result in significant fines, penalties and litigation awards

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth identified on February 21, 2024 that cybercrime threat actors had gained access to certain Change Healthcare systems.
required_facts.evidence: on February 21, 2024, we identified that cybercrime threat actors had gained access to certain Change Healthcare information technology systems.

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth estimates that approximately 190 million individuals were impacted by the Change Healthcare cyberattack.
required_facts.evidence: We have determined the estimated total number of individuals impacted by the Change Healthcare cyberattack is approximately 190 million.

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth provided interest-free loans to care providers in response to the Change Healthcare cyberattack.
required_facts.evidence: To support care providers we provided interest-free loans of more than $9 billion through December 31, 2024.

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth incurred direct response costs for the Change Healthcare cyberattack in 2024.
required_facts.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2024, we incurred $2.2 billion of direct response costs

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth's Optum Insight lost revenue from business disruption caused by the Change Healthcare cyberattack in 2024.
required_facts.evidence: Optum Insight also experienced estimated business disruption impacts of $867 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, reflecting lost revenue

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth says future risks from the Change Healthcare cyberattack, including litigation, reputational harm and regulatory actions, could adversely affect its financial condition or results.
required_facts.evidence: It is possible that future risks and uncertainties resulting from the Change Healthcare cyberattack, including risks related to impacted data, litigation, reputational harm, and regulatory actions could adversely affect our financial condition or results of operations.

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth says that as of December 31, 2024 it had not identified any risks from cybersecurity threats that have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect it.
required_facts.evidence: As of December 31, 2024, the Company has not identified any risks from cybersecurity threats that have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect the Company

required_facts.fact: UnitedHealth's cybersecurity program is overseen by the Audit and Finance Committee of its Board of Directors.
required_facts.evidence: The Audit and Finance Committee of the Board of Directors has oversight of our cybersecurity program

cases.question: Compare the supply chain risks of Apple and NVIDIA.
cases.notes: Apple's latest 10-K is FY2025 (year to September 2025), followed by a Q1 FY2026 10-Q reporting no material changes; NVIDIA's is FY2025 (year to January 2025), followed by three 10-Qs, the latest of which restates every updated risk factor. Rewritten for version 2 from the whole supply passages of each Risk Factors Section. The comparison rests on what both name: outsourced manufacturing concentrated in Asia and trade restrictions.

required_facts.fact: Apple says a significant majority of its manufacturing is performed by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam.
required_facts.evidence: A significant majority of the Company’s manufacturing is performed in whole or in part by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam

required_facts.fact: Apple says obtaining certain components from single or limited sources subjects it to significant supply and pricing risks.
required_facts.evidence: Because the Company currently obtains certain components from single or limited sources, the Company is subject to significant supply and pricing risks.

required_facts.fact: Apple says restrictions on international trade, such as tariffs, can materially adversely affect its business and supply chain.
required_facts.evidence: Restrictions on international trade, such as tariffs and other controls on imports or exports of goods, technology or data, can materially adversely affect the Company’s business and supply chain.

required_facts.fact: Apple relies on partners primarily located in Asia for final assembly of substantially all of its hardware products.
required_facts.evidence: on partners primarily located in Asia, for final assembly of substantially all of the Company’s hardware products

required_facts.fact: Apple says its outsourcing arrangements reduce its direct control over production and distribution.
required_facts.evidence: they also reduce the Company’s direct control over production and distribution

required_facts.fact: Apple says its new products often use custom components available from only one source.
required_facts.evidence: the Company’s new products often utilize custom components available from only one source

required_facts.fact: Apple says many of its components are at times subject to industry-wide shortages and significant commodity pricing fluctuations.
required_facts.evidence: Many components, including those that are available from multiple sources, are at times subject to industry-wide shortages and significant commodity pricing fluctuations

required_facts.fact: Apple says global supply chains can be highly concentrated, so an escalation of geopolitical tensions could cause significant disruptions.
required_facts.evidence: Global supply chains can be highly concentrated, and an escalation of geopolitical tensions or conflict could result in significant disruptions.

required_facts.fact: Apple says trade restrictions can increase the cost or limit the availability of its products, components, rare earths and other raw materials.
required_facts.evidence: Restrictive measures can increase the cost or limit the availability of the Company’s products and the components and rare earths and other raw materials that go into them.

required_facts.fact: Apple reports that new U.S. tariffs, including on imports from China and India, were announced beginning in the second quarter of fiscal 2025.
required_facts.evidence: Beginning in the second quarter of 2025, new tariffs were announced on imports to the U.S. (“U.S. Tariffs”), including additional tariffs on imports from China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the European Union (“EU”), among others.

required_facts.fact: Apple's first-quarter fiscal 2026 10-Q reports no material changes to its risk factors since its 2025 Form 10-K.
required_facts.evidence: There have been no material changes to the Company’s risk factors since the 2025 Form 10-K.

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA says its business depends on consistent and reliable supply from overseas partners, especially in Taiwan and South Korea.
required_facts.evidence: Finally, our business depends on our ability to receive consistent and reliable supply from our overseas partners, especially in Taiwan and South Korea.

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA depends on foundries to manufacture its semiconductor wafers.
required_facts.evidence: We depend on foundries to manufacture our semiconductor wafers using their fabrication equipment and techniques.

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA does not assemble, test or package its products itself but contracts with independent subcontractors.
required_facts.evidence: We do not assemble, test, or package our products, but instead contract with independent subcontractors.

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA lists the limited number and geographic concentration of its suppliers, foundries and contract manufacturers among its supply risks.
required_facts.evidence: limited number and geographic concentration of global suppliers, foundries, contract manufacturers, assembly and test providers and memory manufacturers

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA says geopolitical tensions involving Taiwan and China, where it has suppliers critical to its supply continuity, could have a material adverse impact on it.
required_facts.evidence: geopolitical tensions, such as those involving Taiwan and China, which comprise a significant portion of our revenue and where we have suppliers, contract manufacturers, and assembly partners who are critical to our supply continuity, could have a material adverse impact on us

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA says export controls have disrupted and could in the future disrupt its supply chain and distribution channels.
required_facts.evidence: Export controls have and could in the future disrupt our supply chain and distribution channels, negatively impacting our ability to serve demand

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA says long manufacturing lead times and uncertain supply, combined with inaccurate demand estimates, have led and could lead to mismatches between supply and demand.
required_facts.evidence: Long manufacturing lead times and uncertain supply and capacity availability, combined with a failure to estimate customer demand accurately, has led and could lead to mismatches between supply and demand.

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA says it has experienced extended lead times of more than 12 months.
required_facts.evidence: We have previously experienced and may continue to experience extended lead times of more than 12 months.

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA has paid premiums, provided deposits and entered into long-term supply agreements to secure future supply and capacity.
required_facts.evidence: To secure future supply and capacity, we have paid premiums, provided deposits, and entered into long-term supply agreements and capacity commitments, which have increased our product costs

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA is increasing its U.S.-based manufacturing to support domestic production.
required_facts.evidence: We are increasing our U.S.-based manufacturing and investing in specialized equipment and processes to support domestic production.

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA says new export controls can leave it with excess inventory and purchase obligations, as it recently experienced with the H20.
required_facts.evidence: resulting in excess inventory and purchase obligations as we recently experienced with the H20

required_facts.fact: NVIDIA's gross margins in the second quarter of fiscal 2025 were hurt by inventory provisions for low-yielding Blackwell material.
required_facts.evidence: our gross margins in the second quarter of fiscal year 2025 were negatively impacted by inventory provisions for low-yielding Blackwell material

cases.question: What are the main risks facing the major banks?

starter.label: What are the main risks facing the major banks?

cases.notes: EDA variant V3. The Sector table's Banks industry is Bank of America and JPMorgan; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are Capital Markets. Bank of America's latest 10-K is FY2024 and its 2025 10-Qs report no material changes. Rewritten for version 2 from each whole Risk Factors Section: each bank's market and economic, regulatory, credit, liquidity and operational risks are must-state, its other risk categories details.

required_facts.fact: Bank of America says it may be adversely affected by the financial markets, fiscal, monetary and regulatory policies, and economic conditions.
required_facts.evidence: We may be adversely affected by the financial markets, fiscal, monetary, and regulatory policies, and economic conditions.

required_facts.fact: Bank of America says it is highly regulated and subject to evolving government legislation and regulations.
required_facts.evidence: We are highly regulated and subject to evolving government legislation and regulations and certain settlements, orders and agreements with government authorities from time to time.

required_facts.fact: Bank of America says economic or market disruptions and insufficient credit loss reserves may result in a higher provision for credit losses.
required_facts.evidence: Economic or market disruptions and insufficient credit loss reserves may result in a higher provision for credit losses.

required_facts.fact: Bank of America says a failure in or breach of its operations or information systems, or those of third parties, could disrupt its businesses and cause legal or reputational harm.
required_facts.evidence: A failure in or breach of our operations or information systems, or those of third parties or the financial services industry, could cause disruptions, adversely impact our businesses, results of operations and financial condition, and cause legal or reputational harm.

required_facts.fact: Bank of America says the Federal Reserve could limit or prohibit its capital actions, such as dividends and share repurchases.

required_facts.fact: Bank of America says a reduction in its credit ratings could limit its access to funding or the capital markets.

required_facts.fact: Bank of America says it and its customers are ongoing targets of an increasing number of cybersecurity threats and cyberattacks.
required_facts.evidence: We, our employees, customers, regulators and third parties are ongoing targets of an increasing number of cybersecurity threats and cyberattacks.

required_facts.fact: Bank of America says changes to international trade and investment policies could negatively impact financial markets globally.

required_facts.fact: Bank of America says it faces significant financial and reputational risks from lawsuits and regulatory and government action.
required_facts.evidence: We are subject to significant financial and reputational risks from potential liability arising from lawsuits and regulatory and government action.

required_facts.fact: Bank of America says it faces significant and increasing competition in the financial services industry.
required_facts.evidence: We face significant and increasing competition in the financial services industry.

required_facts.fact: Bank of America's Q3 2025 10-Q reports no material changes from the risk factors in its 2024 Form 10-K.

required_facts.fact: JPMorgan lists legal and regulatory risks, including the impact of extensive supervision and regulation, among its principal risk factors.
required_facts.evidence: Legal and Regulatory risks, including the impact of extensive supervision and regulation

required_facts.fact: JPMorgan lists credit risks, including adverse changes in the financial condition of clients and counterparties, among its principal risk factors.
required_facts.evidence: Credit risks, including the effects from adverse changes in the financial condition of clients, customers, counterparties, central counterparties and other market participants

required_facts.fact: JPMorgan lists liquidity risks, including the potential effect of credit rating downgrades on its liquidity and cost of funding.
required_facts.evidence: the potential adverse effects that any downgrades of JPMorganChase’s credit ratings could have on its liquidity and cost of funding

required_facts.fact: JPMorgan lists market risks, including the effects of changes in interest rates and credit spreads, among its principal risk factors.
required_facts.evidence: Market risks, including the effects that unfavorable economic and market events and conditions, political developments, changes in interest rates and credit spreads, and market fluctuations could have on JPMorganChase’s businesses

required_facts.fact: JPMorgan says its ability to distribute capital to shareholders could be limited if it does not satisfy regulatory capital requirements.
required_facts.evidence: Capital risks, including the risk that JPMorganChase’s ability to distribute capital to shareholders or to support its business activities could be limited if it does not satisfy applicable regulatory capital requirements.

required_facts.fact: JPMorgan says future security breaches due to cyber attacks are inevitable.
required_facts.evidence: JPMorganChase has experienced security breaches due to cyber attacks in the past, and future breaches are inevitable.

required_facts.fact: JPMorgan says its businesses could be negatively affected by economic uncertainty resulting from political and geopolitical developments.
required_facts.evidence: JPMorganChase’s businesses could be negatively affected by economic uncertainty resulting from political and geopolitical developments.

required_facts.fact: JPMorgan says it can be vulnerable to competition from firms that are less regulated or unregulated.
required_facts.evidence: A highly-regulated financial services firm such as JPMorganChase can be vulnerable to competition from firms that are less regulated or unregulated.

required_facts.fact: JPMorgan says its operations and competitive standing could be adversely affected by the development of advanced technologies such as AI.
required_facts.evidence: JPMorganChase’s operations, results, and competitive standing could be adversely affected by the development of advanced technologies such as AI.

cases.question: What AI-related risks do the major software companies describe?
cases.notes: The Sector table's Software industry is Adobe, Microsoft, Oracle and Salesforce. Their latest fiscal years end in November 2025, June 2025, May 2025 and January 2025; Microsoft alone has later 10-Qs, the latest of which (Q2 FY2026) restates its risk factors with new AI passages. Rewritten for version 2 from every AI passage in each Risk Factors Section: each Company's headline AI risk is must-state, its competition, regulation, cost and intellectual property risks details.

required_facts.fact: Adobe says there can be no assurance that its new or enhanced AI solutions will be successful, adopted or monetizable.
required_facts.evidence: there can be no assurance that our new or enhanced solutions and AI innovations will be successful, adopted or monetizable

required_facts.fact: Adobe says issues relating to the development and use of AI in its solutions may result in reputational harm and liability.
required_facts.evidence: Issues relating to the development and use of AI in our solutions may result in reputational harm, liability and adverse business and financial results.

required_facts.fact: Adobe says it faces increasing competition from companies offering generative and agentic AI solutions.
required_facts.evidence: we face increasing competition from companies offering generative and agentic AI solutions

required_facts.fact: Adobe says some of its operations are subject to the EU AI Act.
required_facts.evidence: Some of our operations are subject to the EU AI Act

required_facts.fact: Adobe says the third-party AI models in its solutions could result in scrutiny and legal liability, including intellectual property infringement claims.
required_facts.evidence: The use and availability of third-party AI models in our solutions could result in scrutiny and legal liability, including intellectual property infringement claims.

required_facts.fact: Adobe says the costs of developing and deploying AI could adversely impact its margins.
required_facts.evidence: These costs could adversely impact our margins as we continue to make significant investments in AI development

required_facts.fact: Adobe says other companies have prevented, limited or interfered with its ability to use third-party models in its solutions.
required_facts.evidence: Other companies have in the past, and may in the future prevent, limit or interfere with our ability to use third-party models in our solutions.

required_facts.fact: Adobe says it may be more difficult to protect its generative AI innovations with patents.
required_facts.evidence: it may be more difficult to protect our generative AI and related innovations with patents

required_facts.fact: Salesforce says the markets and monetization strategies for Agentforce and Data Cloud remain relatively new and uncertain.
required_facts.evidence: the markets and monetization strategies for certain offerings, including Agentforce and Data Cloud, remain relatively new and uncertain

required_facts.fact: Salesforce offers Agentforce and Data Cloud through a consumption-based business model.
required_facts.evidence: we offer certain products, including Agentforce and Data Cloud, through a consumption-based business model

required_facts.fact: Salesforce says it has limited experience determining optimal pricing for its consumption-based contracts.
required_facts.evidence: We have limited experience with determining optimal pricing for our consumption-based contracts.

required_facts.fact: Salesforce says social and ethical issues, including the use or capabilities of AI in its offerings, may result in reputational harm and liability.
required_facts.evidence: Social and ethical issues, including the use or capabilities of AI in our offerings, may result in reputational harm and liability.

required_facts.fact: Salesforce says the known risks of generative AI include accuracy, bias, toxicity, privacy and security, and data provenance.

required_facts.fact: Salesforce says competitors may incorporate AI into their offerings more efficiently or successfully than it can.

required_facts.fact: Salesforce says the large language models used in its AI offerings may not remain available at reasonable prices or on commercially reasonable terms.
required_facts.evidence: The hardware, software, data and cloud computing platforms that we rely on, including, for example, the large language models leveraged in our AI offerings, may not continue to be available at reasonable prices, on commercially reasonable terms or at all.

required_facts.fact: Salesforce says its use of AI may expose it to copyright infringement claims related to AI training or output.
required_facts.evidence: the use or adoption of AI technologies in our products and services may expose us to copyright infringement or other intellectual property misappropriation claims related to AI training or output

required_facts.fact: Microsoft says issues in the development, deployment and use of AI may result in reputational or competitive harm or liability.
required_facts.evidence: Issues in the development, deployment, and use of AI may result in reputational or competitive harm or liability.

required_facts.fact: Microsoft says it is incurring significant costs to build and maintain infrastructure for cloud-based and AI services, reducing its operating margins.

cases.question: How dependent are the aerospace and defense companies on U.S. government contracts?
cases.notes: The Sector table's Aerospace & Defense industry is Boeing, Lockheed Martin and RTX, all with FY2025 10-Ks. Rewritten for version 2 from each Risk Factors Section's government contract passages, plus RTX's Business Section, which gives the share of its sales made to the U.S. government (version 1 left it out). The dollar amounts have no SEC company-facts value for these Companies, so the facts state shares, not amounts.

required_facts.fact: Boeing earned 35% of its 2025 revenues under U.S. government contracts, including Foreign Military Sales.
required_facts.evidence: In 2025, 35% of our revenues were earned pursuant to U.S. government contracts, which include FMS.

required_facts.fact: Boeing says the U.S. government may modify, curtail or terminate its contracts without prior notice, at its convenience or for default.
required_facts.evidence: The U.S. government contracting party may modify, curtail or terminate its contracts and subcontracts with us, without prior notice and either at its convenience or for default based on performance.

required_facts.fact: Boeing says funding under its U.S. government contracts may be reduced or withheld in the Congressional appropriations process.
required_facts.evidence: funding pursuant to our U.S. government contracts may be reduced or withheld as part of the U.S. Congressional appropriations process

required_facts.fact: Boeing's BDS and BGS defense businesses each generated approximately 60% of their 2025 revenues from fixed-price contracts.
required_facts.evidence: Our BDS and BGS defense businesses each generated approximately 60% of their 2025 revenues from fixed-price contracts.

required_facts.fact: Boeing's non-U.S. customers, including Foreign Military Sales through the U.S. government, accounted for 46% of its 2025 total revenues.
required_facts.evidence: In 2025, non-U.S. customers, which include Foreign Military Sales through the U.S. government (FMS), accounted for 46% of our total revenues

required_facts.fact: Lockheed Martin derived 72% of its 2025 consolidated sales from the U.S. Government.
required_facts.evidence: We derived 72% of our total consolidated sales from the U.S. Government in 2025

required_facts.fact: Lockheed Martin derived 63% of its 2025 total consolidated sales from the Department of War, also known as the Department of Defense.
required_facts.evidence: including 63% from the Department of War (DoW), also known as the Department of Defense

required_facts.fact: Lockheed Martin expects to continue to derive most of its sales from U.S. Government contracts.
required_facts.evidence: We expect to continue to derive most of our sales from work performed under U.S. Government contracts.

required_facts.fact: Lockheed Martin says government shutdowns and continuing resolutions can affect the amount and timing of funding for its programs.
required_facts.evidence: Budget uncertainty, extended or repeated U.S. Government shutdowns, the use of continuing resolutions, and the federal debt ceiling can adversely affect our industry and both the quantum and timing of funding for our programs.

required_facts.fact: Lockheed Martin's F-35 program, its largest, represented 27% of its 2025 total consolidated sales.
required_facts.evidence: is our largest program and represented 27% of our total consolidated sales in 2025

required_facts.fact: Lockheed Martin says 28% of its 2025 total sales were associated with international customers.
required_facts.evidence: In 2025, 28% of our total sales were associated with international customers.

required_facts.fact: RTX says U.S. government sales constitute a significant portion of its consolidated sales.
required_facts.evidence: U.S. government sales constitute a significant portion of our consolidated sales.

required_facts.fact: RTX's sales to the U.S. government, excluding foreign military sales, were 38% of its total net sales in 2025.
required_facts.evidence: Sales to the U.S. government as a percentage of total net sales(1) (2) |  | 38 | % |  | 40 | % |  | 46 | % (1)    Excludes foreign military sales through the U.S. government.

required_facts.fact: RTX's sales to the U.S. government fell from 46% of its total net sales in 2023 to 38% in 2025.
required_facts.evidence: Sales to the U.S. government as a percentage of total net sales(1) (2) |  | 38 | % |  | 40 | % |  | 46 | %

required_facts.fact: RTX says the U.S. government is its largest customer, representing a substantial majority of its total defense sales.
required_facts.evidence: The U.S. government is our largest customer, representing a substantial majority of our total defense sales.

required_facts.fact: RTX says changes in U.S. government defense spending could negatively impact its financial position and results of operations.
required_facts.evidence: Changes in U.S. government defense spending could negatively impact our financial position, results of operations, liquidity, and overall business.

required_facts.fact: RTX says its U.S. government contracts generally permit the government to terminate them at its convenience or for default.
required_facts.evidence: U.S. government contracts with prime contractors generally permit the government to terminate the contract, in whole or in part, without prior notice, at the U.S. government’s convenience or for default based on performance.
